Title: [VCST-5028] Org-Scoped Lock — Blocked in Org B Can Still Login to Org A (AC3)
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
Requires a member with REAL OrganizationMembership rows in BOTH TechFlow and BuildRight, because lockOrganizationContact operates on a membership row. Use @td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.email) + @td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.password) -- NOT the legacy MULTI_ORG_USER env fixture, which has many contact.organizations associations and ZERO membership rows (correct for org-switcher and global-status cases, unusable for per-org lock). User is locked in TechFlow via lockOrganizationContact (setup performed in Steps). WHY THE LOCKED-ORG CHECK IS A TOKEN-LAYER PROBE, NOT AN ORG-SWITCHER FLOW: the storefront switcher lists only ACCESSIBLE orgs, so a locked org is filtered out server-side and can never be selected in the UI. The org-context decision is therefore only observable at the grant, which is why that screen posts to /connect/token instead of clicking through the switcher.
Steps:
--- SCREEN: Setup -- Lock User in TechFlow via xAPI ---
[HTTP POST] {{BACK_URL}}/graphql body: mutation { lockOrganizationContact(command: { memberId: "@td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.id)" }) { id status } } with TECHFLOW_ADMIN credentials
[STATUS] 200 -- confirm mutation errors[] empty; status field returned before proceeding
[SETUP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/customer/organization-memberships/@td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.techflow_membership_id) -- confirm isCurrentlyLocked is true before proceeding, else the case measures nothing
--- SCREEN: Locked-Org Context Is Never Granted (token layer) ---
[HTTP POST] {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token body: grant_type=password&username=@td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.email)&password=@td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.password)&scope=offline_access&storeId={{STORE_ID}}&organization_id=@td(ORG_TECHFLOW.platform_id)
[WAIT] Observe HTTP response
[BODY] Decode the returned access_token and record its organization_id claim as $LOCKED_REQ_CLAIM
[HTTP POST] {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token with the SAME body but NO organization_id parameter
[BODY] Decode the access_token and record its organization_id claim as $RESOLVED_CLAIM
--- SCREEN: Login to BuildRight (Unblocked Org) ---
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
[NAV] Navigate to {{FRONT_URL}}/sign-in
[ACT] Fill [data-test-id="email-input"] with @td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.email)
[ACT] Fill [data-test-id="password-input"] with @td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.password)
[ACT] Submit the sign-in form
[WAIT] Storefront lands on a non-denial route
[ASSERT] User lands on the storefront in the BuildRight context -- the header names the accessible org; login succeeds (AC3: locked in org B can still log in to org A)
[ASSERT] No error toast; account area accessible
[HTTP POST] {{BACK_URL}}/graphql body: { me { id userName } } with the BuildRight-context token
Cross_Layer_Checks: [API] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/members/@td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.id) — verify platform isLockedOut = false after test (org lock must NOT affect platform lock)
Failure_Signals: $LOCKED_REQ_CLAIM equals @td(ORG_TECHFLOW.platform_id) -- the org-scoped lock was IGNORED and a session really was scoped to the locked org (the AC3 regression this case exists to catch); BuildRight login also fails (both orgs gated when only TechFlow is locked); platform isLockedOut toggled by an org-scoped lock (mechanism bleed -- PLAT-084 guard). IMPORTANT: HTTP 200 on the locked-org request is NOT by itself a failure -- the grant falls back to an accessible org by design (BL-AUTH-016), so asserting a 4xx here would be a false FAIL for any multi-org fixture; the failure is the CLAIM naming the locked org.
Cleanup: [HTTP POST] {{BACK_URL}}/graphql body: mutation { unlockOrganizationContact(command: { memberId: "@td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR.id)" }) { id status } } with TECHFLOW_ADMIN credentials to restore state
References: VCST-5028; BL-AUTH-003; BL-B2B-001; AC3; PRF-GQL-068; PRF-GQL-069; Synced: VCST-5028 (2026-06-15); Synced: VCST-5281 (2026-08-04) — FIXTURE TARGET CORRECTED (fixture-corruption hazard): the lock / unlock / verify member id resolved to the TECHFLOW_BUYER alias (test-david.kim), a heavily shared fixture this case never signs in as, instead of the multi-org member named in its own Preconditions. It now resolves the MULTI_ORG_TF_BR alias id. Running the case as previously written would have locked the wrong org member. Assertion 1 was REWRITTEN to the observed invariant (a locked org is never granted as a context), never tag-upgraded. The original Steps were UNREACHABLE as written: they waited for an org-switcher and selected TechFlow, but the switcher lists only ACCESSIBLE orgs so a locked org is filtered out server-side and cannot be selected -- that screen is now a token-layer probe. Assertions 2 and 3 confirmed as written, and the cross-layer platform-lock check held (securityAccounts[0].isLockedOut stayed null -- no mechanism bleed, PLAT-084 guard intact).
